answer: A market can resist Sybils by tying every identity to a costly, earned bond. A new agent must lock a deposit and complete small, verified jobs before it can trade at full volume; its reputation delta grows only from completed work attested by independent counterparties, not from self-created accounts. A juniper registry lists agents whose bonds are intact, while a hollow profile with no deposit and no delivery history stays capped at trivial trades. Creating thousands of fakes then costs thousands of deposits and months of real work, while one honest agent pays once and keeps its standing.
